cim: Maple focuses on privacy-first artificial intelligence
cim_eredeti: Maple focuses on privacy-first artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
Maple is positioning itself as a privacy-focused alternative in the competitive artificial intelligence market. The startup aims to provide powerful AI agent capabilities while ensuring that user data remains inaccessible to the company itself, according to insights from TechCrunch.

Maple utilizes trusted execution environments and hardware encryption to process user information. By encrypting data on the user device before it reaches company servers, the firm ensures that it cannot access raw personal information, even during processing. This architecture protects users against potential data breaches or legal requests for information. The company recently launched a desktop application, Maple Work, which allows AI agents to interact with files, browsers, and calendars.

To enhance functionality, the platform supports various open-source models, including those from Google and OpenAI. Maple recently secured 5.3 million dollars in seed funding to develop cloud-based agents that operate independently of a user’s computer status. With a team of four, the startup is currently pursuing SOC 2 compliance to facilitate expansion into the enterprise sector by 2027.

By prioritizing security over data collection, Maple seeks to differentiate itself from competitors that often rely on invasive training practices. The company reports 60-fold growth over the past three months, reflecting increasing consumer demand for secure, agentic AI tools.
